SI-4_title.answer: Delineating the Heterogeneity of Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment Using Normative Models of Dynamic Brain Functional Networks

NM2-1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used Gaussian process regression (GPR) for normative modeling to predict dynamic functional connectivity features using sex and age as covariates. GPR was chosen for its ability to handle nonlinear relationships and provide robust estimation of predictive uncertainty. Sex-specific normative age models were constructed.
NM2-1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We estimated normative models to predict each dFC feature using sex and age as covariates in Gaussian process regression (17,32) in a large healthy reference cohort from dataset 1. Gaussian process regression is grounded in a distribution over functions, facilitating Bayesian nonparametric interpolation. This approach ensures robust fitting for nonlinear relationships among variables and delivers consistent estimation of predictive uncertainty (33).
NM2-1_modeling_methods.location: Huo2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Normative Modeling for a-FCS and f-FCS

NM2-2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled two types of dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) features derived from resting-state fMRI: (1) average functional connectivity strength (a-FCS) - the average value of overall functional connections within each Yeo-17 network across all time windows; (2) fluctuation characteristic of connection strength (f-FCS) - the average change of the frame-wise variation of the strengths. Each participant's dFC pattern was represented by 34 features (17 a-FCS and 17 f-FCS for each Yeo-17 network).
NM2-2_response_variable.supporting_text: For each Yeo-17 network, we calculated the average functional connectivity connection strength (a-FCS) and its fluctuation (fFCS, average change of the framewise variation of the strengths) from dFC matrices (Supplemental Method S3). In this way, each participant's dFC pattern was represented by 34 features.
NM2-2_response_variable.location: Huo2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Identification of dFC Features

NM2-3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative models were constructed using sex and age as covariates (predictors) in the Gaussian process regression framework. Sex-specific normative age models were built, meaning separate models were trained for males and females.
NM2-3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We estimated normative models to predict each dFC feature using sex and age as covariates in Gaussian process regression (17,32) in a large healthy reference cohort from dataset 1.
